title: The elbow plot
text: Inertia is how far games sit from their group's centre, added up. More groups always lowers it, so you look for the bend where extra groups stop paying off. The curve here bends gently with no sharp elbow, which is the first sign the games do not form natural clumps. The dashed line is the default, k = 4.

title: Choosing k
text: Blue asks whether games sit closer to their own group than the next one; it is low at every k (above 0.5 would be clear groups). Orange refits on random halves of the games and checks the answers agree. It stays above the dotted 0.85 line up to k = 4, then the groups stop being repeatable. That is why 4 is the default.

title: The game types on the scoreboard
text: Each dot is a game placed by its halftime score and coloured by the type k-means gave it. The X marks are the group centres. The colours meet edge to edge with no empty space between them: the model is drawing borders across one cloud, not finding islands. (Yards also count, so a few dots sit in a neighbour's area.)

title: Silhouette plot
text: One thin bar per game, grouped by type. Bars reaching right are games that clearly belong; bars near zero sit on a border; bars pointing left are closer to another group's games. The dashed line is the average, 0.25. Every group has a long tail toward zero, which is the border games.

title: How each type finishes
text: Average final score for the games in each type, with the share that went over their pregame total. The dashed line is the all-games average. The model never saw these results, so the gaps between bars are the evidence that the groups mean something.
